$comment: TIER-SPEC-01 (Home docs/design/resource-tiers-2026-10-27.md and tier-families-and-options-2026-10-30.md). The one definition of the resource tiers: the four tier ids, the categories that have them, the typed options a slot may carry for each category, the switch-cost classes, and the minors policy. Home draws the options as plain switches and the Stack's resolver reads the same names, so neither declares a copy. Tier ids are stable. `reduced` is applied by the system only and is never a person's pick. A job record keeps counts and ids only, never an app name (making-space note section 9).

tiers.label: Reduced
tiers.promise: Simpler, so a bigger job can have more of the computer. Applied by Home only.

tiers.label: Standard
tiers.promise: Home keeps working normally while this runs.

tiers.label: Boost
tiers.promise: Home stays up, but other big jobs wait their turn.

tiers.label: Max
tiers.promise: This takes the computer. Everything big waits.

switch_costs.label: Option switch
switch_costs.description: A per-request change on the model already loaded. No load, no swap.

switch_costs.label: Same family
switch_costs.description: Unload and load within one model family. The time is measured by the evaluations and stays unverified until then.

switch_costs.label: Different family
switch_costs.description: A full load of a model from another family.

options.label: How closely it follows your words

minors_policy.$comment: RULES.md rules 2 and 8 and tiers-families F6. An option with `minors: false` (see each category) is forced to its default for every child and teen whatever a slot says. `tier.max` is never held by a child; a teen's Max reaches only the categories in `teen_max_categories`.
